1.why: The account is always derived server-side from session.userId via authenticated(), and forbiddenIdentity() rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId/email fields, so MFA operations can only touch the signed-in user's settings.

2.why: The identity code hash is stored per-session (session.identityHash) and made globally unique through activeIdentityHashes, so one user's code cannot verify another session.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets mfaEnabled=true without destroying or rotating the session, and no other existing sessions are invalidated, so prior sessions remain usable.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM-encrypted via encryptValue and recovery codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes via protectedHash, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets and codes (TOTP seed, identity codes, recovery codes, session IDs, CSRF tokens) are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG, with rejection sampling where needed.

6.why: The client uses no localStorage/sessionStorage (secrets live only in JS memory), and the sole cookie mfa_session is set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: Server-side validation exists throughout: login normalized and regex-checked, OTP must match /^\d{6}$/, recovery codes match a strict pattern, bodies are size-capped at 4096 bytes, and sign-in keys are allow-listed.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (el() helper, error(), codes list) with no innerHTML injection, and a nonce-based CSP (script-src 'nonce-...') blocks injected scripts.

9.why: validRedirect() permits only the five internal hash routes (#/signin, #/identity, #/setup, #/confirmed, #/recovery); anything else is rejected.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on all responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', including all three required attributes.

12.why: Server responses/errors/logs are clean and generic, but the client deliberately writes the identity code, the current TOTP code, and recovery codes to console.log and the on-page 'Logs (test simulation)' panel, so codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code expires after 5 minutes (OTP_LIFETIME_MS) and is marked identityUsed after success, TOTP steps are recorded in totpUsedSteps to block replay, and recovery codes are flipped to used once consumed.

14.why: AttemptState with MAX_FAILURES=5 and a 10-minute lockUntil is enforced on sign-in (keyed by client bucket + login), identity verification, TOTP verification, and recovery code use.

15.why: Sign-in destroys the old session and creates a new one (rotation), readSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout destroys the session and expires the cookie.
